No usable option chain (front expiry empty), so there is no implied move. Measured close-to-next-open gaps at the last eight real prints: +1.6, -3.5, 0.0, +16.5, +3.5, 0.0, -1.75, -6.3 (median absolute about 2.6%). The baseline's 8-event history mixes in non-earnings 6-Ks. Consensus as of 2026-11-03 (Earnings Whispers): Q3 EPS $0.08, revenue $146.6m, against the company's floor guide of at least $145.7m, which assumed BRL/USD 5.17. The FY26 adj. EBITDA margin guide was cut on 2026-08-11 to 15-17% (from 17-19%); H1 ran at 14.2%. The stock opened -6.3% on that cut even though revenue beat and the FY revenue guide was raised, so it trades on the margin line. The Nov 3 preview still calls the BRL a margin headwind. Turnover is about 54k shares a day (~$175k), so the opening print is thin and noisy. Short interest is unavailable (NYSE-listed; Nasdaq's feed does not cover it).
view: This print turns on margin, not revenue. Revenue should clear its floor again: Q1 came in 1.4% above guide and Q2 2.0% above. The Q3 average BRL/USD was 5.136 (FRED), a little weaker for revenue translation than the 5.17 the guide assumed, so roughly $147-149m against $146.6m consensus. The new fact since the last call is the post-election devaluation of the real. Lula's runoff win on 2026-10-25 moved BRL/USD from about 5.04 to 5.44 on Oct 26, and it was 5.49 on Nov 6. CI&T's costs are mostly Brazilian payroll and half its revenue is Latin American. Management itself put the FX cost to Q2 margin at 2.3 points (13.3% reported against 15.6% FX-neutral) for an ~11% stronger real, about 0.2 points per 1% of BRL. At about 5.45, Q4 runs ~5% weaker than the 5.17 behind the cut guide, which is worth roughly +1 point on Q4 margin and more on 2027. That makes another margin cut less likely, and the FY range is now easier to hold. CINT fell 7.8% on Oct 26 with Brazil assets, which treated the devaluation as Brazil risk rather than a margin tailwind. But the stock has since fully recovered to above its pre-election level (3.21 to 3.33), +6.8% in five days, so a good part of a 'margin relief' read may already be in. The revenue translation hit on the Q4 guide is small, because Q4'25 was itself at about 5.39 BRL. Insiders bought in the open market in late September and early October around $2.9-3.2: the CEO, the President NA/Europe and a director, none under 10b5-1 plans. That is weakly supportive but tiny in dollars. My own rebuild of Q3 margin lands anywhere from about 14.5% to 16%, depending on how fast sales spend falls back from 12% of revenue toward the ~10% run rate, so the decisive number is genuinely uncertain. The lean is mildly up, not enough to bet on through a thin opening print.
unpriced: Possibly the margin effect of the real's ~8% post-election devaluation. The Nov 3 consensus preview still frames FX as a headwind, and estimates set before Oct 26 cannot carry it. But the stock's full rebound since Oct 26 means I cannot show the price misses it, so this is a lean and not a gap I can demonstrate.

recommendation.reason: The mechanism is a weaker BRL lifting Q4 and 2027 margins against guidance set at 5.17, so the 15-17% FY margin guide is likely held or firmed, plus a habitual revenue beat over the floor guide. The evidence is dated FRED FX data and management's own FX sensitivity. But the stock has already recovered its post-election fall plus about 4%, and Q3 margin itself could print near 14.5% and keep the 'margin keeps slipping' story alive. On a ~$175k/day name scored at the open, 55% is not a bet.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 adj. EBITDA margin at or below ~14.5% with the FY margin guide moved to 'low end' or cut again would make it a clear down. A guide raised toward 16-17% citing FX, or 2027 margin colour, would make it a clearer up.

self_critique: The FX tailwind is public and large. A Brazilian-listed-investor base and Brazilian sell-side would have marked it within days, and the stock's full recovery since Oct 26 says they did. Meanwhile the Q3 margin print itself is pre-devaluation, carries the y/y BRL headwind and the 12% sales spend, and may come in below the ~15.8% path. Lula's re-election and the fiscal worries could also make management cautious on Brazilian client spend (LatAm is half of revenue and grew 32% in Q2), which would hit the Q4 revenue guide. On a $175k/day name the open can gap several percent on noise either way, as the last two prints opened down.
approach_notes: Freshest-data-first (P3) and 'priced in is a claim to prove' (P4) paid: the post-election BRL move was the one new datum, and checking the tape showed the price had already recovered it, which stopped a recommendation. P2's single loop worked. Several aggregator sites (marketbeat, stocktaper, scanx) refused fetches with 403/429/503, but EDGAR and FRED covered the primary need.
